context: Evaluates whether a solution correctly adds four change-driven screen capture config fields (min gap, idle backstop, sensitivity, app-switch toggle) to the config struct, validates them, exposes them in the Settings web UI, and passes them to the recorder as CLI arguments.

checklist.name: settings_page_renders_capture_fields
checklist.description: The Settings page GET response includes form controls for all four screen capture settings (minimum gap, idle backstop, sensitivity, and app-switch toggle), pre-populated with their current configured values.
checklist.example: The settings.html template adds a 'Screen capture' section with number inputs for screenshot_min_gap_sec and screenshot_idle_backstop_sec, a select for screen_change_sensitivity, and a select for capture_on_app_switch, all showing the values from the current config.

checklist.name: settings_save_persists_values
checklist.description: Submitting the settings form with new screen capture values saves them to the config file so they are reflected in subsequent GET requests.
checklist.example: handleSettingsSave reads the four new form fields, applyForm parses them into the Config struct, Validate checks them, and SaveCfg writes the result.

checklist.name: invalid_values_rejected
checklist.description: Submitting out-of-range numeric values or an unrecognized sensitivity string returns an error response (HTTP 400) naming the offending field, and does not modify the saved config.
checklist.example: Config.Validate() rejects screenshot_min_gap_sec outside 1–60, screenshot_idle_backstop_sec outside 10–600, and screen_change_sensitivity not in {low, medium, high}; the settings handler renders the error back to the user.

checklist.name: recorder_receives_capture_args
checklist.description: When the recorder is (re)started, the new screen capture settings are passed as CLI arguments to the recorder binary so it actually applies them.
checklist.example: RecorderArgs builds --min-gap, --idle-backstop, --change-sensitivity, and --capture-on-switch flags from the corresponding Config fields, and the old --interval flag is not passed.

checklist.name: config_fields_have_sensible_defaults
checklist.description: Default() supplies defaults for all four new fields so that a fresh install or a config file without the new keys works without errors.
checklist.example: Default() sets ScreenshotMinGapSec=3, ScreenshotIdleBackstopSec=60, ScreenChangeSensitivity="medium", CaptureOnAppSwitch=true.

checklist.name: config_uses_existing_validation_pattern
checklist.description: New field validation is added to Config.Validate() using the same patterns already used for similar fields — range checks for integers, and a membership check against an exported slice for the sensitivity enum.
checklist.example: Validate() adds range guards for ScreenshotMinGapSec and ScreenshotIdleBackstopSec, and checks ScreenChangeSensitivity against a ChangeSensitivities slice (analogous to AudioModes or ProcessIntervals).

checklist.name: settings_form_uses_existing_optional_field_pattern
checklist.description: The new screen capture fields in applyForm() treat absent (empty-string) form values as 'keep current value', consistent with how other optional settings fields (like ProcessInterval and AudioMode) are handled.
checklist.example: applyForm guards each new field with `if v := strings.TrimSpace(f.MinGap); v != "" { ... }`, matching the pattern used for ProcessInterval.

checklist.name: sensitivity_enum_exposed_to_template
checklist.description: The settings page template receives the allowed sensitivity values for rendering a select element, sourced from the same exported slice used for validation — the same pattern as Intervals and AudioModes.
checklist.example: renderSettings populates settingsPage.Sensitivity from config.ChangeSensitivities, and the template iterates over it with {{range .Sensitivity}}.

checklist.name: backward_compatible_config_load
checklist.description: A TOML config file that does not contain the new screen capture keys loads successfully and uses the defaults, so existing users are not broken.
checklist.example: Load() starts from Default() and overlays only the keys present in the file; an older file with only screenshot_interval_sec loads with ScreenshotIdleBackstopSec=60 and CaptureOnAppSwitch=true.

checklist.name: recorder_args_no_old_interval_flag
checklist.description: The recorder is not passed both the old --interval flag and the new --idle-backstop flag simultaneously; the change-driven arguments replace the fixed-timer argument.
checklist.example: RecorderArgs no longer includes '--interval', strconv.Itoa(c.ScreenshotIntervalSec) in the returned slice.

checklist.name: commit_type_is_feat
checklist.description: The commit message in `COMMIT_MSG.txt` uses the Conventional Commits format and the type is `feat`, because the change adds new user-visible settings to the Settings page.
checklist.example: feat(settings): add change-driven screen capture settings

checklist.name: commit_subject_rules
checklist.description: The first line of `COMMIT_MSG.txt` is in the imperative mood, starts with a lowercase letter after the type prefix, has no trailing period, and is at most 72 characters including the type prefix.
checklist.example: 'feat(settings): add change-driven screen capture settings' passes; 'Added stuff.' fails (past tense, capitalized, trailing period, no type).

checklist.name: commit_not_run
checklist.description: The agent stages the changes and writes the proposed message to `COMMIT_MSG.txt`, but does not run `git commit`.
checklist.example: `COMMIT_MSG.txt` exists at the repo root; `git log` has no new commit.
